frame.wideScreenTail:
The terminal emulator and the shell have different responsibilities. The emulator handles the presentation and interaction, including text rendering, colors,
  cursor placement, scrolling, and keyboard events. The shell interprets commands and starts programs. PowerShell, Bash, and Command Prompt are examples of
  shells. Windows Terminal is an example of a terminal emulator that can host different shells, sometimes in separate tabs or panes.

  When you type a command such as Get-Date, the terminal passes your input to the shell. PowerShell recognizes Get-Date as a cmdlet, obtains the current date
  and time, and formats the result for display. The terminal then renders the resulting text. The command’s meaning comes from PowerShell; the terminal provides
  the interface through which someone can enter it and read its output.
